old: First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform. Not experiencing an inner voice or image isn’t, by itself, resistance or a missing adult capacity. Correct an explicitly unwanted invitation. If you recognize a protective part, you can talk to it:
new: Do you know what exactly feels fake - the words, an image, what you are expecting, the role etc? It doesn't matter that you don't have an inner voice/image to do this, it isn't about not having a 'grown up' or resisting doing the work. If it feels like you are being asked to do something you don't want to do then correct this. It could be that there is a part that is protecting you from doing this, so talk to it.

old: “What are you protecting me from?” “Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?” “Are you afraid this is performance?”
new: You could say something like 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid this will just be a performance?'

old: The voice may be the inherited parent enforcing an old belonging rule. Don’t argue with it. Ask which rule it is enforcing and what ordinary evidence would make the new adult voice more believable.
new: It could also be an inner voice of a parent that you are picking up, and it is trying to enforce a rule about how you should be to belong to them. Again, it isn't useful to argue with this part, but find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable 'grown up' voice.

old: The fake feeling can also mean that a needed adult capacity isn’t available yet. Stop demanding a convincing voice. If you can already observe what is happening, borrow the particular warmth, boundary, or direction you lack. A real or imagined caring figure can help. Try one believable sentence or action and see how it is received.
new: If the fake feeling is telling you that you don't have the 'grown up' ability to do this yet, then don't try and convince yourself by using an inner voice. As long as you have enough observing ego to do this, try and borrow what you need from someone who you can imagine is 'good enough' to lend it to you. This could be a family member, friend, famous person etc. Borrow what you need, e.g. warmth, boundary, direction etc. Try out something which rings true to you, whether it is a sentence, an action etc, and see how you get on.

old: Intensity then gets mistaken for meaning. Sometimes the inner child is finally speaking. Sometimes a Protector is showing fear, or shame, grief, anger, longing, and other buried material are asking for care. But an intense state can also be bodily overload, environmental chaos, sleep deprivation, or plain confusion. A frightening image isn’t automatically truth, a bad feeling isn’t automatically a lesson, and a “download” doesn’t deserve belief merely because it came with excellent lighting.
new: Intensity is often assumed to mean it must be significant: the inner child is talking to the conscious self; a Protector is revealing how scared s/he is underneath; shame, grief, anger or longing are ready to be healed. But sometimes intense states are just overload in the body, a chaotic environment, a lack of sleep, or confusion. Just because it looks scary doesn’t mean it’s true. Just because it feels bad doesn’t mean it’s useful. Just because the lighting was excellent doesn’t mean the download is to be believed.
